title: The Hindu Code Bill: Sacrificing Cabinet Office for Women's Rights
summary: A rare and principled act in parliamentary history: Dr. Ambedkar resigned his cabinet office as India's first Law Minister over the stalled Hindu Code Bill, prioritizing women's equal rights over political power.
keywords: The Hindu Code Bill: Sacrificing Cabinet Office for Women's Rights
full_text:
Following independence, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar assumed office as independent India's first Law Minister in Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet.

His crowning legislative initiative was the **Hindu Code Bill**—a landmark reform aimed at codifying and reforming personal law to protect women's rights:
1. Daughters were to receive an equal share in ancestral property alongside sons.
2. Polygamy was to be outlawed, establishing strict monogamy.
3. Women were granted the legal right to petition for divorce from abusive marriages.
4. Inter-caste marriages and adoptions were legally recognized.

However, conservative members inside and outside parliament raised intense opposition, filibustering the bill and warning of disruptions to traditional family structures.

Faced with strong resistance and the looming 1952 general elections, Prime Minister Nehru chose to postpone the comprehensive legislation.

Ambedkar addressed Parliament with fiery conviction:
"Honorable members! You gladly grant succession rights to the heirs of rajas and maharajas; why do you hesitate at the thought of granting equal property rights to your own daughters?
A husband is free to abandon his wife, yet some demand that an abused woman must suffer without legal recourse!
How can a nation boast of constitutional freedom when half its population remains legally disenfranchised?"

When the government decided not to press forward with the complete bill in that session, Ambedkar took a principled step.

In September 1951, he submitted his resignation as Law Minister.

In his resignation statement, Ambedkar recorded:
"I did not enter this government for office or ministerial status. I came to secure justice for the oppressed and to bestow equal rights upon the women of India.
Since the government cannot steer this vital measure through parliament, my conscience forbids me from continuing in office!"

Ambedkar took the extraordinary step of resigning his cabinet post on principle to champion the cause of women's equal rights. In subsequent years, Parliament enacted the core principles of the Hindu Code across several landmark statutes (including the Hindu Marriage Act of 1955 and Hindu Succession Act of 1956), vindicating his vision.
moral: Power and office are meaningful only as instruments for justice; walking away from power when principles are compromised is the mark of supreme integrity.
witty_quote: I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved!

He wanted to move to England
He was appointed to the Supreme Court
